newsitem.title: USA: Arctic expectations drive NYMEX natgas to new high.
newsitem.headline: Arctic expectations drive NYMEX natgas to new high.

text.p: Expectations that an Arctic air mass will sweep into the U.S. from Canada this week helped drive NYMEX January Henry Hub natgas futures up 16 percent Monday to a new all-time high, industry sources said.

January, which rallied to a new all-time high of $4.56 per million British thermal units, finished 61.6 cents higher at $4.467. February also hit a new benchmark of $3.92, then closed up by 46.9 cents at $3.884. Others also ended higher.
"Bitter cold weather and low inventories - we don't have an inventory cushion, so people are opting to buy now instead of using their insurance (stocks)," said a Houston trader.
Temperatures over most of the nation are expected to plunge to 15 degrees F below-normal or colder this week, as an Arctic air mass from Canada sweeps into the Midwest.
And despite a 38 percent surge in five sessions, traders said a lingering Arctic mass this month could keep the bears on the defensive for a while.
"If wells start freezing up, you'll definitely see more upside. The only people selling it are people who own it," a trader said, adding some freeze ups were likely based on recent forecasts.

Technical traders said January resistance was difficult to peg, with the spot month now in uncharted territory, but some saw next resistance in the $4.95 area based on a swing measurement. Support was seen in the low-to-mid $3.50s and then at $3.19.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices surged about 40 cents Monday to the $4 level. Midcontinent pipes were at least 50 cents higher at about $4. Gas at the New York city gate was talked in the $4.40 area, also up almost 50 cents.
The 12-month strip jumped 16.9 cents to $2.731. NYMEX said 45,878 Hub contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 40,707.
NYMEX January Alberta natgas finished seven cents higher at $1.75, while February ended up four cents at $1.65. NYMEX said seven Alberta lots traded versus two on Friday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded for the thirteenth consecutive day. January settled 77 cents higher at $4.02.
On the KCBT, January ended 63 cents higher at $4.30, while deferreds closed up by 4.5 to 37.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.4 cents to 16.7 cents (NYMEX premium).
